title: Progress Tracking Gaps and Orchestrator Aggregation Research Finding

tldr.content: The current change is documentation-only, tracker-off by default, and covers 12 of 14 skills. Address the request with a versioned executable progress projection keyed to compiled route nodes, default-on output policy across all 14 skills, and durable CAS/fencing persistence separate from telemetry and receipts.

executiveSummary.content:
The repository already has strong orchestration identity, retry, cursor, receipt, telemetry, and SQLite mechanisms, but no numeric progress authority. The correct shape is:

```text
compiled selected route nodes -> logical progress items -> attempts/receipts/evidence
                                      -> durable progress snapshot
                                      -> operator tracker projection
telemetry --------------------------> correlated observation only
```

Progress must aggregate selected logical work, not catalog entries, event counts, nested skill bars, or retry attempts. Default-on behavior is a public output change and must be adopted deliberately by every skill, including the two currently uncovered skills.

keyFindings.content:
K1. supported: The current tracker is prose-only, OFF by default, and present in 12/14 skill definitions; csm-browse and csm-upload have no tracker contract. [ref-repo-tracker] [ref-browse] [ref-upload]

K2. supported: csm-orchestrate already has stable compiled route-node IDs, child-run IDs, retry attempts, durable cursors, receipts, and correlated telemetry, but no executable progress aggregate. [ref-compiler] [ref-orchestrate] [ref-cursor] [ref-telemetry]

K3. supported: The safest logical aggregation unit is one selected compiled route node per graph revision; retries remain separate attempts and do not add denominator or completion credit. [ref-compiler] [ref-retry]

K4. supported: Progress snapshots must be separate from telemetry and terminal receipts. They may drive display and recovery visibility, but must not decide gates, retries, or VERIFIED status. [ref-receipt] [ref-telemetry]

K5. partially-supported: Default-on tracking for all skills is feasible as an instruction/output contract, but it is a breaking behavior change for standalone skills and especially for browser/publication workflows. [ref-repo-tracker] [ref-browse] [ref-upload]

K6. supported: Graph revision, remediation insertion, parallel CAS updates, stale writers, and terminal receipt disagreement require explicit progress tests and versioned persistence. [ref-remediation] [ref-store] [ref-tests]

detailSections.content:
## Current contract

The shared tracker text says output is suppressed unless explicitly requested and requires 3–6 milestones with weights totaling 100%. It does not define activation parsing, milestone identity, verified-fraction measurement, or a binding to actual run state. The stronger csm-deep-research wording is an outlier rather than a suite-wide implementation.

The exact current inventory is 14 catalog skills, with tracker text in 12 root/payload pairs. csm-browse and csm-upload remain uncovered. Root and packaged copies are synchronized for the changed orchestrator document, but synchronization is not enforced by a dedicated tracker contract gate.

## Executable model

Add a separate `csm-progress/1` progress document or event/snapshot contract rather than adding arbitrary fields to receipt v2, whose schema is closed to unknown top-level properties. A minimal item is:

```text
ProgressDocument: progressId, runId, graphRevision, items, revision, updatedAt
ProgressItem: itemId, phaseId, nodeId, skill, weight, state, verifiedFraction, attempt, childRunId, evidenceRefs, receiptId, blocker
```

The logical item key is `(runId, graphRevision, phaseId, nodeId)`. The compiled `nodeId` is reused; do not key by skill name because a skill may appear in multiple phases or remediation routes. Item states should distinguish pending, active, verified, failed, blocked, and incomplete. A retry increments attempt and creates a new child run ID while retaining the same logical item.

## Aggregation

Let `S` be the selected route nodes in the compiled graph, including committed remediation nodes for the current graph revision. Let each node have a positive immutable weight, defaulting to 1.

```text
completion = sum(weight(node) * completion(node)) / sum(weight(node))
```

Only `verified` contributes successful completion credit. Failed, blocked, incomplete, running, and selected-but-undispatched nodes contribute zero, remain visible, and have separate counts. Parallel siblings each contribute once. Attempts, child receipts, gates, reviews, stages, telemetry events, and inactive catalog skills are not additional denominator items. Empty selected work is `indeterminate`, not 0% or complete.

Maintain separate projections: plannedProgress over selected `S`; observedWork over dispatched/reconciled nodes; success/outcome status from child results plus gates/review; eventsObserved from telemetry. A failed branch must not disappear from the denominator merely because later branches were never dispatched.

## Lifecycle and authority

Create progress as pending when the route graph is compiled. Transition to active before dispatch, update attempt and child lineage on retry, and mark verified only after child completion, evidence reconciliation, required gates, and review accept it. Mark blocked for policy/approval/reconciliation blockers and incomplete for timeout, missing evidence, or unresolved execution. The parent receipt remains terminal authority; progress never independently produces VERIFIED.

Persist snapshots with `saveProgress(snapshot, expectedRevision, fencingToken)` and load them through the existing durable store boundary. Parallel updates must merge or reject stale revisions deterministically. A missing or stale snapshot must not corrupt cursor recovery; telemetry loss must not prevent progress recovery. Graph revision changes append or remap only according to an explicit remediation policy, preserving completed lineage and adding new weighted items exactly once.

## Skill-wide contract

If default-on is required, replace the current OFF-by-default wording in all 14 root and payload skill definitions with a canonical default-on contract. Define a universal three-to-six milestone shape, skill-specific milestone names, explicit weights, state symbols, truthful unknown handling, scope-change recording, and suppression only when a user explicitly requests quiet output. For csm-browse and csm-upload, retain their safety/publication boundaries and ensure progress never exposes credentials, session data, or publication secrets.

The orchestrator should render the aggregate and per-route skill items from the progress document. Standalone skills should render their own declared milestones; when invoked by the orchestrator, the parent supplies the run/phase/node identity and consumes the child’s progress as evidence, without allowing a child to mutate parent state directly.

recommendation.content: Recommend a staged implementation: first define and register `csm-progress/1` plus a canonical default-on tracker contract and all-14 root/payload parity tests; next integrate progress creation and transitions into compiled route-node dispatch, retry, reconciliation, gates, review, remediation, and terminal paths; then add CAS/fencing persistence and reload/recovery tests; finally add operator rendering and standalone skill output tests. Keep progress snapshots separate from receipt v2 and telemetry. Do not average skill-card percentages or event counts. Before enabling default-on output, explicitly accept the standalone output compatibility change and define quiet-output behavior.

unverifiedClaims.content:
U1. The repository does not yet define whether weights should remain equal forever or later reflect comparable effort; equal weights are a safe initial policy, not a standard.

U2. The exact default-on activation and quiet-output mechanism is a user-facing contract decision; the current `--progress` convention implies opt-in and must be replaced or inverted deliberately.

U3. Whether csm-browse and csm-upload should expose progress during external browser/publication side effects needs explicit safety review; universal coverage is requested but output must not leak sensitive operational data.

U4. A progress snapshot schema, registry entry, store API, and concrete implementation do not yet exist. This finding defines the smallest viable shape but does not prove compatibility with every existing store adapter.

U5. Full assistive-technology behavior is not established by text-contract or structural tests alone.

processAppendix.content: Tier: DEEP. Source mode: local. Four independent read-only tracks covered tracker contract coverage/defaults, runtime entities and persistence seams, aggregation/failure/retry semantics, and testing/packaging parity. An independent challenger tested the proposed shared schema/default-on/selected-node design and identified the breaking default-on boundary, graph-revision/remediation weighting, attempt identity, CAS/fencing, receipt authority, and schema-registry requirements. A separate judge scored the draft reasoning: factual accuracy 0.68, citation accuracy 0.62, completeness 0.74, clarity 0.84. The judge also surfaced a coverage-count disagreement; direct repository inspection confirms 12/14 tracker-bearing skills because csm-browse and csm-upload lack the section. The judge's claim that all 14 root files contain the tracker was rejected as inconsistent with direct reads of those two files. Research was read-only; no source, configuration, plan, dependency, or external system was changed by the research work. Existing worktree changes were pre-existing plus the single run-owned research artifact created at SAVE. The recommendation retains the user's default-on goal but marks its compatibility and safety consequences as an explicit contract decision rather than assuming it is behavior-neutral.
